DIAGNOSIS READY: Tuberculosis

Please note that based on the clinical history provided—a premature newborn with immediate onset of respiratory distress, grunting, and retractions—the overwhelming medical evidence points to Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) or Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN), not Tuberculosis. Tuberculosis is highly unlikely to present with these specific acute symptoms in a newborn immediately after birth unless there is active, untreated maternal disseminated disease at the time of delivery, which was not indicated in the history.
